text:
Anna (support): FYI Lighthouse reporting high 429s on their Dedicated pool during a scheduled promo. They say tokens/s SLO hit and sustained latency. customer says 'we're seeing timeouts at ~4pm PST'.

Marc (eng): Are they hitting burst credits or admission window? Any recent config changes on their pool?

Anna (support): No config changes reported. I pulled recent events: deploy-bot posted a prewarm at 15:55 but then a sudden spike at 16:03. Logs show admission drops. Snippet: ```admission_controller: deny request account_id=acct_lighthouse reason=burst_credit_exhausted tokens=1200```

Sasha (oncall): Pulling admission metrics now. Querying admissions per-minute for acct_lighthouse.

Sasha (oncall): Quick find: burst_credit_balance dropped to 0 at 16:02:41, admission headroom set to 250 tps, incoming load jumped to ~700 tps for ~35s, autoscaler didn't add nodes until 16:03:25.

Priya (ml): That timing smells like prewarm not keeping up with the extreme tail. What's the pool's autoscale policy? min=2 max=10 scale_window=30s?

Tony (sre): Pool config: dedicated-pool-11, min_replicas=2, max_replicas=8, scale_up_cooldown=20s, target_util=0.75. The initial surge likely saturated KV cache warmups and GPU slots. Autoscaler added +2 at 16:03:30 but admission already throttled many requests.

Alex (cs): Customer timeline: they doubled marketing emails at 15:59; first error at 16:02. They expect guidance on mitigation and a timeline to prevent recurrence.

Marc (eng): Root hypotheses: 1) burst credits drained because token-per-second consumed faster than projected; 2) autoscaler scale-up latency + cold KVCaches cause sustained high per-request latency so admission controller keeps denying; 3) noisy neighbor? Check per-account session distribution across replicas.

Sasha (oncall): I'm grabbing per-replica admission logs + per-account token counters. Command I ran: ```SELECT replica, account_id, sum(tokens) FROM admissions WHERE time >= '2023-07-08T16:00:00Z' AND time <= '2023-07-08T16:06:00Z' GROUP BY replica, account_id;```

Sasha (oncall): Results: acct_lighthouse dominated tokens on replicas r3,r4 (70% of load) while r1,r2 had unrelated tenants (noisy neighbor = other tenant with batch translations). r3/r4 hit token ceilings first.

Priya (ml): That indicates uneven routing; the router should spread sessions to reduce hot-spotting. Any route affinity rules?

Tony (sre): There's sticky-routing enabled for session affinity on that pool for low-latency customers. Seems it backfired during the spike. We need to consider temporary affinity relaxation during high burst windows.

Marc (eng): Immediate mitigation steps we can take now: 1) manual refill of burst credits for acct_lighthouse to allow short-term acceptance; 2) temporarily relax session affinity to rebalance; 3) increase admission headroom threshold (from 250 to 400) for the pool while autoscaler catches up; 4) recommend customer apply client-side pacing. Which do we want to run asap?

Alex (cs): Customer asks for the fastest fix. Manual burst refill + relaxing affinity sounds good. Also they'll accept guidance on client pacing.

Tony (sre): I'll do a manual burst refill of +2000 tokens and relax affinity flag for 10 minutes. Executing: ```/admin/burst_refill acct_lighthouse 2000 --reason "marketing surge" && /pools/patch dedicated-pool-11 --set "session_affinity=false" --ttl 600```

deploy-bot: ran /admin/burst_refill acct_lighthouse 2000 -> success. ran /pools/patch dedicated-pool-11 -> success.

Sasha (oncall): After changes, admission denies dropped to near zero and 95th latency improved from 1.6s -> 0.45s within 30s. Autoscaler added 2 replicas by 16:04:00 and another at 16:04:50.

Priya (ml): Follow-up: we should add proactive headroom guidance for customers with planned blasts: a formula like min_headroom = peak_expected_tps * safety_factor(1.2) + kv_warmup_margin. Also add an automatic affinity relaxer when detected burst > X for Ys.

Marc (eng): Agreed. Action items: (1) build an autoscale prewarm plan for scheduled events (CS integration) (owner: Marc), (2) implement temporary affinity relaxation heuristic in router (owner: Tony), (3) add alert that correlates burst_credit_balance nearing zero + rapid tps increase (owner: Sasha), (4) update runbook for support to run refill + patch (owner: Anna).

Anna (support): I'll notify customer and provide suggested client-side pacing example: ```backoff: if http 429 -> wait 200ms * retry_count until < 10 retries; cap throughput to 300 tps during window``` and share postmortem in the next 24h.

Alex (cs): Customer grateful for quick response. They requested us to schedule a follow-up to tune Dedicated pool for recurring promotions. I'll set that up.

Marc (eng): Quick note for noisy neighbor: we should add per-replica accounting in autoscaler decisions so heavy single-account concentration triggers more aggressive scaling.

Sasha (oncall): Logging this thread in incident tracker and tagging "dedicated-admission" "burst-credits" "noisy-neighbor".

Tony (sre): Implemented a short-term monitor: if one account consumes >60% tokens on a pool for >15s, trigger rebalancer + alert. Rolling out in canary now.

Anna (support): Closing loop with customer and will attach logs + TTL of burst refill. Closing thread once CS follow-up scheduled. :white_check_mark:
